passages.text: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again, and it is a safeguard for you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
Paul calls them his brothers.
Paul tells them to rejoice in the Lord.
Paul says he repeats the same instructions to them.
Paul says it is not difficult for him to write these things again.
Paul says these repeated instructions keep them safe.
passages.original: Τὸ λοιπόν ἀδελφοί μου χαίρετε ἐν Κυρίῳ τὰ αὐτὰ γράφειν ὑμῖν ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρόν ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές

passages.text: Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!
passages.sermon:
Paul warns the believers in Philippi.
He tells them to watch out for certain people.
These people are dangerous.
They act like dogs.
They do evil work.
They mutilate the flesh.
Paul calls them "dogs," "evil workers," and "mutilators."
He wants the believers to be careful of such people.
passages.original: Βλέπετε τοὺς κύνας βλέπετε τοὺς κακοὺς ἐργάτας βλέπετε τὴν κατατομήν

passages.text: For it is we who are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God, who glory in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in the flesh— though I myself could have such confidence. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee; as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to righteousness in the law, faultless.
passages.sermon:
We are the true people of God.
We are the circumcision.
We worship God by His Spirit.
We boast in Christ Jesus.
We do not put confidence in human effort.
I am Paul.
I could have confidence in human effort.
If anyone else thinks he has reason to trust in the flesh, I have more.
I was circumcised on the eighth day.
I am from the people of Israel.
I belong to the tribe of Benjamin.
I am a Hebrew, born of Hebrews.
I followed the law as a Pharisee.
I was zealous.
I persecuted the church.
I was faultless in righteousness based on the law.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς γάρ ἐσμεν ἡ περιτομή οἱ Πνεύματι Θεοῦ λατρεύοντες καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐν σαρκὶ πεποιθότες καίπερ ἐγὼ ἔχων πεποίθησιν καὶ ἐν σαρκί Εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἄλλος πεποιθέναι ἐν σαρκί ἐγὼ μᾶλλον περιτομῇ ὀκταήμερος ἐκ γένους Ἰσραήλ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων κατὰ νόμον Φαρισαῖος κατὰ ζῆλος διώκων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ γενόμενος ἄμεμπτος

passages.text: But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Jewish man.
Paul was a Pharisee.
Paul once valued many things.
Paul thought these things were gains.
Paul now follows Christ.
Paul considers all his former gains as loss.
Paul does this for the sake of Christ.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη ταῦτα ἥγημαι διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν ζημίαν

passages.text: More than that, I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a follower of Jesus Christ.
Paul values knowing Christ Jesus above everything else.
Paul calls Jesus Christ his Lord.
Paul considers all things to be loss compared to knowing Christ Jesus.
Paul has lost all things for the sake of Christ.
Paul considers everything he lost to be worthless.
Paul wants to gain Christ.
Paul wants to be found in Christ.
Paul does not want to have his own righteousness.
Paul’s own righteousness would come from the law.
Paul wants the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ.
This righteousness comes from God.
This righteousness is based on faith.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ μὲν‿ οὖν‿ γε καὶ ἡγοῦμαι πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου μου δι’ ὃν τὰ πάντα ἐζημιώθην καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύβαλα ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ νόμου ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ τὴν ἐκ Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει

passages.text: I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death, and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul wants to know Christ.
Paul wants to know the power of Christ’s resurrection.
Paul wants to share in Christ’s sufferings.
Paul wants to become like Christ in His death.
Paul hopes that, by doing this, he will reach the resurrection from the dead.
passages.original: τοῦ γνῶναι αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν κοινωνίαν τῶν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ συμμορφιζόμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ εἴ πως καταντήσω εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: Not that I have already obtained all this, or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking as a follower of Jesus Christ.
Paul has not already obtained all these things.
Paul has not already been made perfect.
Paul presses on.
Paul wants to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of him.
passages.original: Οὐχ ὅτι ἤδη ἔλαβον ἢ ἤδη τετελείωμαι διώκω δὲ εἰ καὶ καταλάβω ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ κατελήμφθην ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Brothers, I do not consider myself yet to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, I speak to you now.
I have not yet taken hold of the goal.
I do not consider myself to have reached it.
But I do one thing.
I forget what is behind me.
I reach forward to what is ahead.
I press on toward the goal.
I want to win the prize.
This prize is God’s heavenly calling.
God gives this calling in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: ἀδελφοί ἐγὼ ἐμαυτὸν οὐ λογίζομαι κατειληφέναι ἓν δέ τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω ἐπιλανθανόμενος τοῖς δὲ ἔμπροσθεν ἐπεκτεινόμενος κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view. And if you think differently about some issue, God will reveal this to you as well.
passages.sermon: All of us who are mature should think this way.\r\nIf you think differently about something, God will show this to you too.
passages.original: Ὅσοι οὖν τέλειοι τοῦτο φρονῶμεν καὶ εἴ τι ἑτέρως φρονεῖτε καὶ τοῦτο ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῖν ἀποκαλύψει

passages.text: Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained.
passages.sermon:
We have already reached a certain level in our faith.
We must live according to that level.
We must not fall below what we have already attained.
We must continue to walk in the way we have learned.
passages.original: πλὴν εἰς ὃ ἐφθάσαμεν τῷ αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν

passages.text: Join one another in following my example, brothers, and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Christian brothers.
Paul urges the brothers to follow his example.
Paul tells them to join together in this.
Paul instructs them to watch those who live as he does.
Paul says these people follow the pattern he and his companions set.
Paul wants the brothers to observe and imitate this pattern.
passages.original: Συμμιμηταί μου γίνεσθε ἀδελφοί καὶ σκοπεῖτε τοὺς οὕτω περιπατοῦντας καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς

passages.text: For as I have often told you before, and now say again even with tears: Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul speaks to the believers.
Paul warns the believers.
Paul says, “Many people live as enemies of the cross of Christ.”
Paul has told the believers this many times before.
Paul now says it again.
Paul says this with tears.
passages.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦσιν οὓς πολλάκις ἔλεγον ὑμῖν νῦν δὲ καὶ κλαίων λέγω τοὺς ἐχθροὺς τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.
passages.sermon:
Many people live as enemies of the cross of Christ.
Their end is destruction.
They serve their own desires as their god.
They take pride in things that bring them shame.
They think only about earthly things.
passages.original: ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες

passages.text: But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ, who, by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself, will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.
passages.sermon:
We are citizens of heaven.
Heaven is our true home.
We wait for a Savior from heaven.
This Savior is the Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ has great power.
His power enables Him to bring everything under His control.
Jesus will use His power to change our bodies.
Our bodies are now lowly and humble.
He will make our bodies like His glorious body.
passages.original: Ἡμῶν γὰρ τὸ πολίτευμα ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει ἐξ οὗ καὶ Σωτῆρα ἀπεκδεχόμεθα Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν ὃς μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ δύνασθαι αὐτὸν καὶ ὑποτάξαι αὑτῷ τὰ πάντα
